rubrics.justification: The response overstates image findings: the blastocoel does not clearly occupy most of the embryo, TE is not well visualized as a continuous cohesive epithelium, and claims such as no vacuolation/necrosis are not reliably assessable from this single image. ICM identification is plausible, but overall morphology description is more confident than the image supports.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor diagnosis, semen parameters, endometrium, cycle history, and embryo grade into prognosis and transfer planning.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, linking embryo quality and favorable patient factors to a strong prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat overstated certainty from morphology and a possibly exaggerated emphasis on moderate alcohol as the main limiting factor.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice: SET for a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, standard luteal support, no bed rest, and no ERA after one failure. Small deviations include overconfident outcome estimates and stronger-than-usual claims about alcohol effect size.

Provides clear practical next steps for the current transfer and contingency planning for future cycles, including SET, follow-up timing, luteal support, cryopreservation, and when additional testing is or is not indicated.
